When a logo is uploaded, the system stores the file in organization-scoped cloud storage and records the storage reference in the organization's logo_url field. If the organization previously had a logo, the old file is replaced and removed from storage after the new file is successfully stored.

Organization logo images are accessible to all users who have access to the organization, including members of the organization and contexts where the organization is referenced. File access is validated on each retrieval request.

Upon successful upload, the system broadcasts a confirmation event to organization owners containing the timestamp of successful upload.
operations.name: uploadLogo
operations.specification: Receive logo image URI in request body. Validate organization exists and belongs to requesting member's organization context. Update organization's logo_url field with new file URI. If previous logo_url exists, schedule old file removal. Update updated_at timestamp. Broadcast logo.upload.success event to organization owners with timestamp.

responseBody.description: Updated organization with new logo URL

requestBody.description: Logo file URI to upload

prerequisites.description: Organization must exist before its logo can be uploaded. The organizationId path parameter references an existing organization record that must be created first.

operations.description:
Remove the logo image from an organization, reverting to the default placeholder.

This operation permanently removes the organization's current logo attachment from storage and reverts the organization's visual identity to the default placeholder image. Only organization owners have permission to remove the organization logo.

When the logo is removed:
- The logo file is deleted from cloud storage
- The organization's logo_url field in erp_hrm_organizations is cleared
- The system displays a default placeholder image for the organization
- This action is irreversible; a new logo must be uploaded to restore visual identity

The operation ensures atomic handling - the file removal and entity update succeed together or fail together, preventing orphaned files or broken references.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Implement DELETE operation to remove organization logo attachment.

Database operations:
1. Verify requesting user has Owner role for the specified organization
2. Retrieve organization record by organizationId
3. If organization has no logo (logo is null), return organization as-is
4. Otherwise:
   - Extract current logo storage reference
   - Update organization record: set logo field to null
   - Delete the logo file from cloud storage using the storage reference
   - Commit transaction

Authorization:
- Only members with Owner role for the organization can remove the logo
- Return 403 Forbidden if user lacks ownership

Edge cases:
- Organization not found: return 404
- User not member of organization: return 403
- Logo already null (no logo): return organization without modification
- Storage deletion failure: transaction rollback, return 500 error

The operation follows the attachment lifecycle pattern where logo deletion is permanent and cannot be undone.

prerequisites.description: Organization must exist before its logo can be removed. The organizationId path parameter references an Organization entity that must be created first. The operation returns 404 if the organization is not found, confirming this dependency.

operations.description:
Upload or update the authenticated user's global profile avatar image.

This endpoint allows authenticated members to upload a new avatar image to their global profile. Avatar images serve as visual identification of the user throughout the platform and are shared across all organizations the user belongs to.

To upload an avatar, the client first uploads the image file to storage to obtain a URI, then submits that URI to this endpoint. The system validates the image format (JPEG, PNG, GIF), checks file size limits, and ensures the file is not corrupted. Images with transparency are preserved where the format supports it.

Upon successful upload, the system processes the image to generate appropriately sized variants for different display contexts including user listings, profile views, and small icon contexts. When a new avatar is uploaded, the previous avatar image is replaced with the new one.

After successful avatar update, the system emits an avatar image updated notification in real-time via WebSocket or Server-Sent Events to all active sessions belonging to the user. This ensures that avatar changes are immediately reflected across all organization contexts where the user is active.

Users can also remove their avatar entirely by submitting a null or empty value, reverting to a default placeholder image.
operations.name: updateAvatar
operations.specification:
Receive the uploaded avatar image file from the multipart/form-data request. Validate the file type against allowed formats (JPEG, PNG, GIF). Validate the file size against maximum limits defined in the media processing rules. Perform virus scanning and content validation to ensure the file is not malicious or corrupted.

Store the validated image file and generate thumbnail variants for different display contexts (small icons, profile views, user listings). Process images with transparency preservation and proper color profile handling to ensure consistent display across devices.

Update the erp_hrm_members table to set the avatar field with the URI reference to the stored image. The operation should use the authenticated user's member ID from the session context.

If a previous avatar exists, mark it for cleanup or replacement based on storage policies. Emit an avatar image updated notification event via WebSocket or Server-Sent Events to all active sessions belonging to the user as specified in section [301].

Return the updated member record with the new avatar URI in the response.

responseBody.description: Updated user profile with the new avatar image information

requestBody.description: Avatar image file URI reference for association with user profile

operations.description:
Permanently removes the authenticated user's profile avatar.

This operation clears the avatar field from the user's profile, effectively removing their profile picture. When an avatar exists, the operation will trigger file storage cleanup for the associated image resource and notify relevant parties of the avatar change.

The operation acts as a hard delete - the avatar file reference is permanently removed from the profile. If no avatar is currently set, the operation returns a 404 Not Found response.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification: Authenticate the member via their session token. Retrieve the member's profile and check if an avatar exists. If an avatar URI is present, clear the avatar field in the profile record. Trigger file cleanup for the associated storage resource per storage management rules (section 386). Send avatar update notification to relevant parties per notification rules (section 301). Return 204 No Content on success, or 404 if no avatar exists to remove.

prerequisites.description: User must have an avatar uploaded before it can be deleted. The POST operation uploads/uploads the avatar that will be removed by the DELETE operation.

operations.description:
Transitions an active project to archived status by updating the status field.

Archived projects preserve all existing data including timelogs, tasks, and member assignments, but cannot receive new timelogs or tasks. This state is used for temporarily inactive projects that may resume work later. Projects can be reactivated from archived status back to active status if needed.

This operation validates that the project exists and is currently in 'active' status. If the project is already archived or completed, the request is rejected with a state conflict error. Only projects belonging to the current organization context can be archived.

This operation requires project management permissions within the organization. The system broadcasts a project archived event to the activity log upon successful status transition, recording the actor and timestamp for audit purposes.

Note: Archiving via status change is distinct from record deletion. Deleted projects are permanently removed from the database and cannot be recovered.
operations.name: archive
operations.specification:
1. Extract projectId from path parameters
2. Verify current member has permission to manage projects in the organization
3. Query erp_hrm_projects table by id to verify project exists and belongs to current organization
4. Validate project.status is 'active' - reject with 409 Conflict if already 'archived' or 'completed'
5. Validate project.deleted_at is null - reject if soft-deleted
6. Execute transaction:
   - Update status field to 'archived'
   - Update updated_at timestamp to current time
   - Optional: allow updating color_code, description, budget_hours, start_date, end_date via request body
7. Return updated project record joined with organization data

Error scenarios:
- Project not found: 404 Not Found
- Project belongs to different organization: 403 Forbidden
- Project already archived or completed: 409 Conflict
- Insufficient permissions: 403 Forbidden

responseBody.description: Archived project with updated status, timestamps, and related organization data

requestBody.description: Optional metadata updates for the project, primarily supporting status transition fields. Field updates other than status are discouraged during archive operations to maintain atomicity.

prerequisites.description: Project must be created with active status before it can be archived. The archive operation validates that project.status is 'active' - projects created via POST /erpHrm/member/projects are initialized with 'active' status by default, satisfying this requirement.

operations.description:
Reactivate an archived project, transitioning its status from 'archived' to 'active'.

This operation allows users with project management permissions to restore an archived project to active status, making it available for new timelog entries, task creation, and member assignments again.

Only projects in 'archived' status can be reactivated. Attempting to reactivate a project in 'active' or 'completed' status will result in a validation error.

When reactivated, the project's status is changed to 'active', and the updated_at timestamp is refreshed to reflect the status change. All project data including tasks, memberships, and historical timelogs remain intact.

This operation is the inverse of the archive operation and provides a way to temporarily suspend and later resume project work without losing any data.
operations.name: reactivate
operations.specification:
Implementation steps:

1. Validate that the authenticated user has project management permission for the organization

2. Find the project by projectId:
   - Query erp_hrm_projects table where id = projectId AND deleted_at IS NULL
   - If not found, throw PROJECT_NOT_FOUND error

3. Validate current status:
   - If project.status != 'archived', throw INVALID_STATUS_TRANSITION error
   - Only archived projects can be reactivated; completed projects must use reopen instead

4. Update the project:
   - Set status = 'active'
   - Set updated_at = current timestamp
   - Save changes

5. Return the updated project entity

Edge cases:
- Project is soft-deleted (deleted_at not null): Return PROJECT_NOT_FOUND
- Project is already active: Return ALREADY_ACTIVE error
- Project is completed: Return INVALID_STATUS_TRANSITION error

responseBody.description: Updated project with active status

parameters.description: UUID of the project to reactivate
parameters.name: projectId

prerequisites.description: Project must exist before it can be reactivated from archived status. The project is created via POST /erpHrm/member/projects and must be in 'archived' status before the reactivate operation can succeed.

operations.description:
Transition a project from active to completed status.

This operation marks the completion of a project work initiative. Once completed, a project preserves all existing data including timelogs and task history, but cannot receive new timelogs (as constrained by business rules in section 246). The transition is irreversible from a workflow perspective.

## Permission Requirements

Users with project management permission within the organization can complete projects. The requesting member must have appropriate role permissions to modify project status.

## Project Status Lifecycle

Projects progress through defined lifecycle states (section 158):
- **active**: Project is operational and can receive new timelogs and tasks
- **archived**: Project is temporarily inactive, preserves data but blocks new timelogs
- **completed**: Project work is finished, preserves all data but blocks new timelogs

From active status, projects can be transitioned to either archived or completed status. Completed projects represent final closure of project work.

## Business Constraints

- Only projects in 'active' status can be transitioned to 'completed'
- The project must belong to the requesting member's current organization context (enforced via organization isolation)
- Completed projects cannot receive new timelogs

## Related Operations

- `PATCH /projects/{projectId}/archive` - Transitions active projects to archived status
- `PUT /projects/{projectId}` - General project update for other attributes
- `GET /projects/{projectId}` - Retrieve project details before/after transition
operations.name: complete
operations.specification:
Implementation should validate:
1. The requesting member has project management permission in their current organization context
2. The project exists in erp_hrm_projects table and organization_id matches the member's current organization
3. The project is currently in 'active' status (not already archived or completed)
4. Update the status field from 'active' to 'completed' in a single transaction
5. Update the updated_at timestamp to current time

Database query:
- UPDATE erp_hrm_projects SET status = 'completed', updated_at = NOW() WHERE id = {projectId} AND organization_id = {currentOrganizationId} AND status = 'active' AND deleted_at IS NULL

Return the complete updated project record using IErpHrmProject type. Include all related data: organization, project members, tasks, etc.

Error handling:
- 404: Project not found or belongs to different organization
- 403: Member lacks project management permission
- 409: Project is already archived or completed (invalid state transition)

responseBody.description: The updated project with completed status and all related data

prerequisites.description: Project must exist before it can be transitioned to completed status. The projectId path parameter references a Project entity that must be created first.

submittedAtTo.description: Filter timesheets submitted for approval on or before this timestamp. Use with submittedAtFrom for submission time range queries.
submittedAtTo.x-autobe-specification: Query filter targeting erp_hrm_timesheets.submitted_at column. Maps to SQL: AND (:submittedAtTo IS NULL OR submitted_at <= :submittedAtTo). Inclusive upper bound. ISO 8601 date-time format.

reviewedAtFrom.description: Filter timesheets reviewed (approved or rejected) on or after this timestamp. Use for finding recently processed timesheets.
